questions.question: Why is helium, a Group 0 element, used to fill balloons rather than hydrogen, despite being slightly heavier?
options: Helium is highly reactive and forms a protective barrier.
Helium is in Group 0, meaning it is unreactive and safe from burning.
Helium is a solid at room temperature and does not leak.
Helium reacts with air to produce water vapour.

questions.question: If you have a sealed container of neon and argon at 25°C (room temperature), what state of matter will both elements be in?
options: They will both be liquids.
One will be a gas and the other will be a liquid.
They will both be gases.
One will be a solid and the other will be a gas.

questions.question: Why do noble gases rarely form chemical bonds with other elements?
options: They have an incomplete outer electron shell, which repels other atoms.
They have complete outer electron shells, making them exceptionally stable.
They are too heavy to collide with other elements.
Their protons are located outside the nucleus, preventing reactions.

questions.question: Helium, neon, argon, and krypton are noble gases listed in order down Group 0. Which of the following trends is correct as you go from helium to krypton?
options: The boiling point decreases.
The density decreases.
The atomic mass decreases.
The boiling point and density both increase.

questions.question: When analyzing the physical properties of elements within a specific group of the periodic table, what general trend is observed?
options: Properties change randomly and unpredictably.
Properties remain absolutely identical for all elements in that group.
Properties change gradually down the group.
Properties alternate between metal and non-metal characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the physical properties and reactivity of Group 1 metals?
options: They are hard, dense, and become less reactive down the group.
They are soft, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive down the group.
They are soft, dense, and become less reactive down the group.
They are hard, low density, and become more reactive down the group.

questions.question: Lithium is added to water containing universal indicator. The indicator turns purple. Which products of the reaction explain this observation and the fizzing?
options: Lithium oxide and oxygen gas.
An alkaline solution of lithium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
An acidic solution of lithium hydride and hydrogen gas.
Neutral water and lithium gas.

questions.question: A student adds a piece of magnesium (a Group 2 metal) to a test tube of dilute hydrochloric acid. What are the products of this chemical reaction?
options: A salt and hydrogen gas.
An alkaline oxide and oxygen gas.
Water and chlorine gas.
Metal hydroxide and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Calcium and potassium are in the same period, but potassium is in Group 1 and calcium is in Group 2. How do their reactivities compare?
options: Calcium is more reactive than potassium, and calcium becomes less reactive down its group.
Calcium is less reactive than potassium, and calcium becomes more reactive down its group.
Calcium and potassium have identical reactivities.
Calcium is more reactive than potassium, but becomes more reactive down its group.

questions.question: If a flask of chlorine gas is opened in a fume cupboard, what would you expect to see, and why must this be done safely?
options: A colourless, harmless vapour that smells like water.
A coloured, toxic vapour that must not be inhaled.
A bright purple solid that melts instantly.
A red liquid that evaporates into an odourless, safe gas.

questions.question: Chlorine, bromine, and iodine are halogens in Group 7, ordered from top to bottom. What are their physical states at room temperature?
options: Chlorine is a solid, bromine is a liquid, iodine is a gas.
Chlorine is a gas, bromine is a liquid, iodine is a solid.
All three elements are gases at room temperature.
All three elements are solids at room temperature.

questions.question: When investigating the displacement reactions of Group 7 elements (halogens), we find that fluorine is extremely reactive, while iodine is much less reactive. What is the trend in reactivity down Group 7?
options: Reactivity increases down the group.
Reactivity remains constant down the group.
Reactivity decreases down the group.
Reactivity decreases then increases down the group.

questions.question: When sodium (Group 1) is heated and placed in a jar of chlorine gas (Group 7), a vigorous reaction occurs to produce a white powder. What is this product?
options: A metal hydride.
A metal halide.
A metal oxide.
A noble gas compound.

questions.question: A student prepares a sample of potassium chloride, which is a metal halide. What will happen if they stir this solid compound into a beaker of water?
options: It will react violently to produce hydrogen gas.
It will dissolve completely because metal halides are soluble in water.
It will remain as an insoluble white precipitate at the bottom.
It will float on top of the water without dissolving.

questions.question: In the modern periodic table, how are columns and rows distinguished?
options: Each column is called a period, and each row is called a group.
Columns and rows are both called groups.
Each column is called a group, and each row is called a period.
Columns are called families, and rows are called categories.

questions.question: Who is credited with the historical development of the periodic table, organizing elements by their atomic weights and properties?
options: Albert Einstein, a German physicist.
Dimitri Mendeleev, a Russian scientist.
Marie Curie, a Polish chemist.
John Dalton, an English schoolteacher.

questions.question: How does the periodic table organize the known chemical elements?
options: Alphabetically by their English names.
Chronologically by the date they were discovered.
Into groups and periods, according to their chemical and physical properties.
Solely by their state of matter at absolute zero.

questions.question: Why are lithium, sodium, and potassium placed in the same column (Group 1) of the periodic table?
options: They have completely different physical properties but identical masses.
They are in the same group because they have similar properties.
They were all discovered in the same year by Mendeleev.
They are all gases that do not react with water.

questions.question: Beyond the numbered vertical groups, how can the elements of the periodic table be broadly categorized?
options: Only into synthetic elements and natural gases.
Into non-metals and metals, which include the transition metals.
Into liquids, solids, and plasma groups.
Into acidic elements and alkaline gases only.

questions.question: A block of an unknown metal can be easily cut with a butter knife and floats on water before reacting rapidly. Which part of the periodic table does this metal most likely belong to?
options: Transition metals, because they are soft and dense.
Group 2 alkaline earth metals, because they have high densities.
Group 1 alkali metals, because they are soft and have low densities.
Group 7 halogens, because they are soft metals.

questions.question: Why are helium and neon used in situations where keeping materials chemically unchanged is critical, such as protecting historical documents or welding?
options: They have high boiling points and density.
They belong to Group 0 and are chemically unreactive.
They form very stable compounds with oxygen at high temperatures.
They are extremely lightweight metals that don't rust.

questions.question: A scientist has four sealed containers of elements from Group 0 (helium, neon, argon, and krypton) at 20 °C. What is the physical state of the substance inside each container?
options: All four are gases.
Helium and neon are gases, while argon and krypton are liquids.
Helium is a gas, but the others are solids.
Helium, neon, and argon are gases, but krypton is a liquid.

questions.question: Why do neon and argon atoms rarely form chemical bonds with other elements?
options: Their outer electron shells are completely full, making them highly stable.
Their nuclei are too small to attract other electrons.
They are too heavy to react with lighter non-metals.
They have an odd number of electron shells that repel other atoms.

questions.question: Moving from neon to xenon down Group 0, which of the following trends correctly describes how their physical properties change?
options: Atomic mass increases, density decreases, and boiling point increases.
Atomic mass increases, density increases, and boiling point increases.
Atomic mass decreases, density increases, and boiling point decreases.
Atomic mass increases, density decreases, and boiling point decreases.

questions.question: If element X is above element Y in the same group of the periodic table, how do we expect their physical and chemical properties to relate?
options: Element Y will have completely different properties that cannot be predicted from X.
Element Y's properties will be identical to those of element X.
There will be a gradual, predictable change in properties from element X to element Y.
Element Y will react with water twice as fast as element X, regardless of the group.

questions.question: A student is comparing a sample of potassium (Group 1) to a sample of iron (a typical transition metal). Which observation is most likely?
options: Potassium is much harder to cut with a knife and has a higher density than iron.
Potassium is soft enough to cut with a knife and has a lower density than iron.
Potassium is harder to cut than iron but floats on water.
Both metals are extremely soft, but iron reacts much more vigorously with cold water.

questions.question: When a small piece of sodium is added to water containing universal indicator, the indicator turns purple and bubbles of gas are produced. What does this reaction demonstrate?
options: Sodium forms an acidic solution and oxygen gas.
Sodium forms an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas.
Sodium forms a neutral solution and carbon dioxide gas.
Sodium forms an alkaline solution and oxygen gas.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is placed into a test tube of dilute hydrochloric acid, bubbles of gas are produced and the metal disappears. What are the products of this reaction?
options: Magnesium chloride (a salt) and oxygen gas.
Magnesium hydroxide (an alkali) and hydrogen gas.
Magnesium chloride (a salt) and hydrogen gas.
Magnesium oxide (a base) and water.

questions.question: Compare the reaction of calcium (Group 2, Period 4) and potassium (Group 1, Period 4) with water. Which statement is correct?
options: Potassium is more reactive than calcium because Group 1 metals are more reactive than Group 2 metals in the same period.
Calcium is more reactive than potassium because reactivity increases as you move right across a period.
Both metals have identical reactivity because they are in the same period.
Calcium is more reactive because Group 2 metals are always more reactive than Group 1 metals.

questions.question: A teacher is demonstrating the properties of chlorine and bromine in a fume cupboard. Why is a fume cupboard necessary for these Group 7 elements?
options: They form colourless, odourless gases that are highly explosive in air.
They are non-metals that produce coloured, toxic vapours.
They are highly reactive metals that burn spontaneously in air.
They release radioactive dust particles into the classroom.

questions.question: Going down Group 7 from fluorine to iodine, what is the correct sequence of their physical states at room temperature (20 °C)?
options: Fluorine (gas), chlorine (liquid), bromine (solid), iodine (solid).
Fluorine (gas), chlorine (gas), bromine (liquid), iodine (solid).
Fluorine (liquid), chlorine (liquid), bromine (solid), iodine (gas).
Fluorine (solid), chlorine (solid), bromine (liquid), iodine (gas).

questions.question: In displacement reactions of halogens, chlorine can displace bromine from sodium bromide, but iodine cannot displace bromine. What does this tell us about the reactivity of Group 7 elements?
options: Reactivity increases down Group 7.
Reactivity decreases down Group 7.
Reactivity remains constant down Group 7.
Reactivity is random and cannot be predicted down Group 7.

questions.question: When heated sodium metal is lowered into a jar of chlorine gas, a vigorous reaction occurs, producing a white solid. What is this white solid?
options: Sodium hydroxide, a metal alkali.
Sodium chlorate, a metal oxide.
Sodium chloride, a metal halide.
Sodium hydride, a metal hydride.

questions.question: A student synthesises three different metal halides: sodium chloride, potassium bromide, and calcium iodide. If they add water to each of these solid compounds, what will they observe?
options: All three metal halides will dissolve because they are soluble in water.
Only the sodium chloride will dissolve; the others will form insoluble precipitates.
None of them will dissolve because metal halides are insoluble in water.
They will react violently with water to release toxic chlorine gas.

questions.question: In the modern periodic table, if two elements are located in the same horizontal row, what can we say about their classification?
options: They are in the same group.
They are in the same period.
They have identical chemical properties.
They must both be non-metals.

questions.question: Which historical scientist is credited with organizing the early periodic table by arranging elements with similar properties together and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements?
options: John Dalton
Dimitri Mendeleev
Ernest Rutherford
Marie Curie

questions.question: How does the modern periodic table assist chemists in predicting the properties of an undiscovered or newly synthesized element?
options: Elements are organized into groups and periods based on their properties, allowing predictions based on their position.
The table lists elements in alphabetical order, so properties are grouped by name.
The table organizes elements solely by their state of matter at room temperature.
Newly synthesized elements always have properties identical to hydrogen.

questions.question: Lithium, sodium, and potassium are all in Group 1. Based on this, which of the following is the most reasonable prediction?
options: They will all have completely different chemical reactions.
They will all react with water in a similar way because they are in the same group.
Potassium will react with water, but lithium will not react at all.
They are in the same group, so they have identical melting points.

questions.question: Aside from vertical groups and horizontal periods, how is the periodic table broadly divided to separate elements like copper and iron from oxygen and helium?
options: Into liquids, gases, and plasmas.
Into natural elements and synthetic elements.
Into metals (including transition metals) and non-metals.
Into reactive solids and unreactive liquids.

questions.question: Two metals, X and Y, are in Group 2. Metal X is below metal Y in the group. How do their reactions with dilute hydrochloric acid compare?
options: Metal X will react more rapidly than metal Y because Group 2 reactivity increases down the group.
Metal Y will react more rapidly than metal X because Group 2 reactivity decreases down the group.
Neither metal X nor metal Y will react because Group 2 metals do not react with acids.
Both metals will react at the exact same rate because they are in the same group.

questions.question: The development of the modern periodic table, which allowed for the prediction of undiscovered elements, is credited to which scientist?
options: John Dalton
Dimitri Mendeleev
Antoine Lavoisier
Ernest Rutherford

questions.question: Helium is used in party balloons because it does not burn or react with oxygen. Which group of the periodic table does helium belong to, and how is this group described?
options: Group 1, which are highly reactive metals
Group 7, which are highly reactive non-metals
Group 0, which are unreactive gases
Group 2, which are moderately reactive metals

questions.question: Xenon and radon are heavy elements located at the bottom of Group 0. What is their physical state under standard room temperature conditions?
options: They are solid metals
They are dense liquids
They are gases
They form a supercooled plasma

questions.question: Why do Group 0 elements, such as neon and argon, rarely form chemical bonds with other elements?
options: They have an incomplete outer electron shell, making them unstable
They have complete outer electron shells, making them stable
Their nuclei are too small to attract other electrons
They exist only as diatomic molecules that cannot be split

questions.question: Going down Group 0 from helium to radon, what trends are observed in their physical properties?
options: Atomic mass, density, and boiling points all increase
Atomic mass increases, but density and boiling points decrease
Atomic mass and density increase, but boiling points decrease
Atomic mass decreases, while density and boiling points increase

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes how physical and chemical properties change within any single group of the periodic table?
options: Properties remain completely identical from the top to the bottom of the group
Properties change gradually as you move down the group
Properties change randomly and unpredictably between adjacent elements
Properties only change when moving from left to right, not down a group

questions.question: A teacher demonstrates cutting a sample of sodium metal with a scalpel. Which set of properties is characteristic of sodium and other Group 1 metals?
options: They are extremely hard, highly dense, and decrease in reactivity down the group
They are soft, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive down the group
They are hard, have very low melting points, and become less reactive down the group
They are soft, have very high densities, and do not react with air or water

questions.question: When lithium is added to water, it fizzes and produces a gas that ignites with a squeaky pop. Why are Group 1 elements known as the alkali metals?
options: They react with water to form an acidic solution and oxygen gas
They react with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas
They react with acids to form an alkaline salt and oxygen gas
They dissolve in water without any chemical reaction to form a neutral solution

questions.question: If a piece of calcium (a Group 2 metal) is added to a beaker of dilute hydrochloric acid, which products will be formed?
options: Calcium chloride (a salt) and hydrogen gas
Calcium hydroxide and chlorine gas
Calcium oxide and hydrogen gas
Calcium chloride (a salt) and oxygen gas

questions.question: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals compare to Group 1 metals in the same period, and how does Group 2 reactivity change down the group?
options: Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals, and reactivity decreases down Group 2
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals, and reactivity decreases down Group 2
Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals, and reactivity increases down Group 2
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals, and reactivity increases down Group 2

questions.question: The elements in Group 7 of the periodic table are known as the halogens. What are the common physical hazards associated with these elements?
options: They are highly reactive metals that produce explosive dust
They are non-metals that produce coloured, toxic vapours
They are inert gases that can cause suffocation by displacing oxygen
They are liquid metals that release highly corrosive acidic fumes

questions.question: If you examine the states of matter of the Group 7 elements at room temperature starting from the top of the group (fluorine) and moving down to iodine, what trend do you observe?
options: They change from gas to liquid to solid
They change from solid to liquid to gas
They are all liquids at room temperature
They are all gases at room temperature

questions.question: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from its halide solution. Which of the following correctly describes the trend in Group 7 reactivity?
options: Reactivity increases down Group 7, making astatine the most reactive
Reactivity decreases down Group 7, making fluorine the most reactive
Reactivity remains constant down the group but depends on temperature
Reactivity decreases down Group 7, making chlorine less reactive than iodine

questions.question: When potassium (Group 1) is reacted with bromine vapour (Group 7), they combine chemically. What is the name of the type of compound formed?
options: Metal hydroxide
Metal halide
Metal hydride
Metal oxide

questions.question: A student prepares a sample of sodium chloride (a metal halide) in the lab. What happens when this compound is added to a beaker of pure water?
options: It remains completely insoluble and forms a solid layer at the bottom
It dissolves completely in the water because metal halides are soluble
It reacts violently with the water to release toxic chlorine gas
It floats on top of the water because it is less dense and insoluble

questions.question: When navigating the periodic table, what are the vertical columns and horizontal rows called?
options: Columns are called periods; rows are called groups
Columns are called groups; rows are called periods
Columns are called families; rows are called blocks
Columns are called categories; rows are called series

questions.question: How are the elements in the modern periodic table arranged to help scientists identify patterns?
options: They are arranged in alphabetical order by their chemical symbols
They are arranged in order of their abundance in the Earth's crust
They are organised into groups and periods according to their properties
They are arranged chronologically by the year they were discovered

questions.question: Why are elements such as fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine all placed together in Group 7 of the periodic table?
options: They have similar properties and react in similar ways
They have the exact same atomic mass and physical state
They were discovered by the same research group in the same decade
They are all highly unreactive gases at room temperature

questions.question: Apart from vertical groups and horizontal periods, how else can the elements in the periodic table be broadly classified?
options: Into soluble elements, insoluble elements, and transition gases
Into metals (which include transition metals) and non-metals
Into radioactive elements and stable synthetic elements
Into acidic elements, basic elements, and neutral compounds

questions.question: Compare magnesium (Group 2, Period 3) and sodium (Group 1, Period 3). Which statement accurately describes their relative reactivity?
options: Magnesium is more reactive than sodium because it has more outer electrons
Magnesium is less reactive than sodium because Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals in the same period
Both metals have identical reactivity because they are located in the same period
Sodium is less reactive than magnesium because sodium is softer and less dense

questions.question: Why is helium (Group 0) used in airships and weather balloons instead of hydrogen, despite hydrogen being lighter?
options: Helium is a metal and does not float easily.
Helium is in Group 0, meaning it has an incomplete outer shell.
Helium is in Group 0 and is unreactive, making it much safer than flammable hydrogen.
Helium readily reacts with oxygen to form a stable, non-flammable compound.

questions.question: Neon and Argon are elements in Group 0. Under standard classroom conditions (room temperature), what physical state would you expect a sample of krypton (also in Group 0) to be in?
options: Liquid, because it is further down the group than neon.
Gas, because all Group 0 elements are gases at room temperature.
Solid, because its atomic mass is much higher than argon.
A mixture of liquid and gas depending on the humidity.

questions.question: Why do elements in Group 0 (the noble gases) not easily form chemical bonds with other elements?
options: They have complete outer electron shells, which makes them highly stable.
They have no electrons in their outer shells, preventing bonding.
They are too small to share electrons with larger elements.
Their nuclei contain too many neutrons, which repels other atoms.

questions.question: Helium (boiling point -269 °C) and Neon (boiling point -246 °C) are the first two elements in Group 0. What is the most reasonable prediction for the boiling point of Argon, the next element down the group?
options: It will be lower than -269 °C, because boiling points decrease down Group 0.
It will be higher than -246 °C, because boiling points increase down Group 0.
It will be exactly -257.5 °C, because it must be the average of the two.
It will be 0 °C, because all other noble gases boil at room temperature.

questions.question: If you observe that fluorine (at the top of Group 7) is a pale yellow gas and chlorine (below it) is a green gas, what does this demonstrate about how physical properties change down a group in the periodic table?
options: Properties change randomly with no predictable pattern.
Properties stay identical for all elements in that group.
Properties change gradually and progressively down the group.
Physical properties only change when moving across a period, not down a group.

questions.question: A student is given a small, dull grey cylinder of a metal. They are able to easily cut it in half with a butter knife, revealing a shiny surface that quickly tarnishes. Which group is this metal most likely from, and what is its reactivity compared to other metals in its group?
options: Group 1, and it is less reactive than the elements below it in the group.
Group 2, and it is more reactive than any other metal in the periodic table.
Group 0, and it is extremely unreactive because it is soft.
Group 7, and its reactivity decreases when cut.

questions.question: When a small piece of sodium is added to a trough of water containing universal indicator, the indicator turns purple and bubbles of gas are produced. What are the products of this chemical reaction?
options: Sodium oxide and oxygen gas.
An acidic solution of sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
An alkaline solution of sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
Sodium chloride solution and water vapour.

questions.question: Magnesium is a Group 2 metal. If a piece of magnesium ribbon is placed into a test tube containing dilute hydrochloric acid, what would you expect to observe and produce?
options: No reaction, because Group 2 metals only react with water.
Bubbles of hydrogen gas and the formation of a soluble magnesium salt.
Rapid production of chlorine gas and a solid magnesium precipitate.
The acid turns into an alkali, producing oxygen gas.

questions.question: Calcium and Magnesium are both in Group 2, while Potassium is in Group 1. Calcium and Potassium are in the same period. Which of the following correctly compares their reactivity?
options: Magnesium is more reactive than Calcium, but less reactive than Potassium.
Potassium is more reactive than Calcium, and Calcium is more reactive than Magnesium.
Potassium is less reactive than Calcium, and Calcium is less reactive than Magnesium.
Magnesium, Calcium, and Potassium all have identical reactivity because they are metals.

questions.question: A lab technician is preparing an experiment using bromine, a Group 7 element. Which safety precaution is most critical based on the general properties of Group 7 elements?
options: Use a fume cupboard because Group 7 elements form toxic, coloured vapours.
Keep it near an open flame because Group 7 elements are highly explosive noble gases.
Handle it with bare hands because Group 7 elements are soft, non-toxic metals.
Keep it in a vacuum because it will react violently with nitrogen gas.

questions.question: Chlorine is a gas at room temperature, while bromine is a liquid. What state would you expect iodine (which is below bromine in Group 7) to be at room temperature?
options: Gas, because states change from solid to gas down Group 7.
Liquid, because all elements in Group 7 are liquids.
Solid, because the state of the elements changes from gas to solid down Group 7.
Plasma, because iodine is highly unstable at room temperature.

questions.question: If chlorine (Group 7) reacts very vigorously with iron wool, and iodine (Group 7) reacts much more slowly with iron wool, what does this tell us about the reactivity trend of Group 7?
options: Reactivity increases down the group, so iodine is more reactive.
Reactivity decreases down the group, so chlorine is more reactive.
Reactivity remains constant, and the difference is due to the state of the iron.
Group 7 elements only react when heated in a vacuum.

questions.question: When sodium (Group 1) is heated and lowered into a jar of chlorine gas (Group 7), a bright yellow flame is seen and a white solid forms. What is this reaction an example of, and what is the product?
options: A halogen reacting with an alkali metal to form a metal halide.
A noble gas reacting with a transition metal to form an alloy.
A Group 2 metal reacting with an acid to form a salt.
A non-metal displacement forming a pure liquid halogen.

questions.question: A student synthesises a sample of potassium bromide (a metal halide). To test its physical properties, they add a small amount of the white solid to a beaker of pure water. What is the most likely outcome?
options: The solid will float on top of the water without changing.
The solid will dissolve completely because metal halides are soluble in water.
The solid will react violently with the water to produce hydrogen gas.
The solid will turn into a toxic purple gas and escape the beaker.

questions.question: In the periodic table, how are the horizontal rows and vertical columns organised and named?
options: Rows are called groups, and columns are called periods.
Rows are called periods, and columns are called groups.
Both rows and columns are called periods.
Both rows and columns are called groups.

questions.question: Who was the Russian scientist responsible for developing the early version of the periodic table, organising elements by their properties and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements?
options: John Dalton
Dimitri Mendeleev
Marie Curie
Ernest Rutherford

questions.question: How does the modern periodic table arrange all the known elements so that chemists can easily study them?
options: In alphabetical order of their chemical names from top to bottom.
By the date they were discovered, starting from ancient times.
Organised into groups and periods according to their properties.
Randomly, with metals on the right and non-metals on the left.

questions.question: If you are told that element X is in the same vertical column (group) as sodium and potassium, what can you most reliably predict about element X?
options: It will have completely different chemical properties to sodium.
It will have similar properties to sodium and potassium.
It will be a dense, unreactive liquid at room temperature.
It will react with water to produce an acidic solution.

questions.question: A materials scientist is categorising a newly synthesised material. It conducts electricity, is shiny, can be hammered into sheets, and is highly dense. Into which broad division of the periodic table should this element be classified?
options: Non-metals
Halogens
Noble gases
Metals, which include the transition metals

questions.question: Argon, Krypton, and Xenon are Group 0 elements. Argon is at the top of this trio, followed by Krypton, then Xenon. If we compare their densities and atomic masses, which of the following statements is true?
options: Argon has the highest atomic mass and the highest density of the three.
Xenon has the highest atomic mass and the highest density of the three.
Krypton has a higher density than Xenon but a lower atomic mass.
All three have identical densities and atomic masses because they are in the same group.
